The '''2017–18 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team''' represented [[Oakland University]] (OU) during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Golden Grizzlies were led by 34th-year head coach [[Greg Kampe]] and played their home games at the [[Athletics Center O'rena]] in [[Rochester, Michigan]] as members of the [[Horizon League]].

Oakland made a three-point field goal in every game of the season, increasing their steak to 937 consecutive games, the eighth-longest active NCAA Division I streak (at the time). They last finished a game without a three-pointer on January 30, 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.goldengrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030518aac.html |title=GOLDENGRIZZLIES.COM :: OAKLAND-CLEVELAND STATE POST GAMES NOTES :: Oakland University Official Athletic Site Oakland University Official Athletic Site :: Men's Basketball |access-date=March 16, 2018 |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316214710/http://www.goldengrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030518aac.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2016–17 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Golden Grizzlies]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 25–9, 14–4 in [[Horizon League]] play to win a share for the Horizon League regular season championship.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/sports/detroit/2017/02/oakland_mens_basketball_takes.html |title=Oakland men's basketball takes 1st Horizon League title, top seed |work=MLive.com |access-date=July 12, 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref> As the No. 1 seed in the [[2017 Horizon League men's basketball tournament|Horizon League tournament]], they were upset in the quarterfinals by [[2016–17 Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball team|Youngstown State]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/watch-horizon-league-favorite-oakland-loses-at-buzzer-to-20-loss-youngstown-state/ |title=WATCH: Horizon League favorite Oakland loses at buzzer to 20-loss Youngstown State |work=CBS Sports |access-date=July 12, 2017 |language=en}}</ref> As a conference champion and No. 1 seed who failed to win their conference tournament, they received an automatic bid to the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2016–17 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]]<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2017/03/14/oakland-stuns-clemson-nit-signature-win/99197034/ |title=Oakland stuns Clemson in NIT for signature win |newspaper=Detroit News |access-date=July 12, 2017 |language=en}}</ref> in the first round before losing to [[2016–17 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]] in the second round.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2017/03/19/oakland-golden-grizzlies-richmond-spiders-nit/99397606/ |title=Oakland's season ends with 87-83 loss at Richmond in NIT |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |access-date=July 12, 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

==Off-season==
===Roster changes===
The Golden Grizzlies lost Sherron Dorsey-Walker, a guard on the [[2016–17 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|2016–17 team]], to graduation. Prior to the season, sophomore Isaiah Brock unexpectedly decided to leave the team. Brock was named to the Horizon League's All-Defensive Team and All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2017/08/09/whos-eligibility-flagged-2016-leaving-oakland-basketball/553251001/ |title=Army vet Isaiah Brock leaves Oakland hoops year after becoming eligible |first1=Nolan |last1=Bianchi |first2=Perry A. |last2=Farrell |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |date=August 9, 2017 |access-date=August 16, 2017}}</ref> Senior guard Stevie Clark also left the team, transferring to [[Louisiana State University in Shreveport]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/sports/college/2017/08/15/lsus-adds-former-okla-state-illinois-state-transfers/570904001/ |title=LSUS adds former Okla. State, Illinois State transfers |first=Jimmy |last=Watson |newspaper=Shreveport Times |date=August 15, 2017 |access-date=August 16, 2017}}</ref>

Oakland was picked by coaches, media and sports information directors to finish first the Horizon League. Oakland received 31 of the 47 votes for first place ahead of second place Northern Kentucky. The adjacent table shows the complete preseason poll. [[Senior (education)|Senior]]s Jalen Hayes and Martez Walker were selected to the preseason first team and [[Kendrick Nunn]] was selected to the second team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://horizonleague.org/news/2017/10/9/mens-basketball-horizon-league-announces-hlmbb-preseason-all-conference-team-poll.aspx?path=mbball|title=HORIZON LEAGUE ANNOUNCES #HLMBB PRESEASON ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM, POLL|website=horizonleague.org}}</ref>

Oakland played three exhibition games, defeating Central Michigan, Rochester College and Davenport in games at the O'rena. The 108–88 victory against Central Michigan was a special game to raise money for the American Red Cross and hurricane relief.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cm-life.com/article/2017/10/mens-basketball-falls-to-oakland-in-hurricane-relief-exhibition-game|title = Men's basketball falls to Oakland in hurricane-relief exhibition game}}</ref>

Oakland received 19 points in the preseason [[Coaches Poll]]<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2017/10/19/msu-hoops-coaches-poll-um-oakland-get-votes/106798712/ |title=MSU hoops No. 2 in coaches poll; UM, Oakland get votes |newspaper=Detroit News |date=October 19, 2017 |access-date=October 19, 2017}}</ref> and 2 points in the [[AP Poll]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2018/poll/1|title = 2017-18 Men's College Basketball Rankings for Preseason}}</ref> ''[[USA Today]]'' named the Golden Grizzlies a team that was "snubbed" by not being ranked in the preseason Top 25.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/10/19/five-teams-snubbed-preseason-mens-basketball-coaches-poll/778467001/ |title=Five teams snubbed in the preseason college men's basketball coaches poll |first=Joe |last=Fleming |newspaper=USA Today |date=October 19, 2017 |access-date=October 19, 2017}}</ref>
